This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with interest.
2.
The petition averments are briefly stated as under:

That on 11.11.2024 at about 6.30 p.m. Sudhindra B.K. was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EG- 7293 at NH-44 Road, in between Reddigollarahalli Cross and Doddapylagurki Cross, Chikkaballapura Taluk, Chikkaballapura, at that time, a driver of APSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.AP-39-UL-6198 drove the bus in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor SCCH 5 cycle, due to the impact of the accident, Sudhindra B.K. sustained severe injuries and succumbed to fatal injuries on the way to the hospital.

Immediately after the accident, body was shifted to Sumitra T L vs Kadiri Vinesh Kumar on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14984316/
2 Government Hospital, wherein post mortem was conducted and body was handed over to the petitioners and they have incurred Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and other incidental expenses.

3. At the time of accident, deceased Sudhindra B.K. @ Sudeendra B.K. was aged about 42 years,
working as Assistant Manage at Eco Mobility, Bengaluru and drawing a salary of Rs.36,101/- p.m.
petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is daughter, petitioner No.3 is mother of the deceased Sudhindra B.K.

Due to death of the deceased, petitioners are undergoing great mental shock,
discomfort and financial loss.
With regard to the accident, case in crime No.190/2024 is registered against SCCH 5 the driver of the APSRTC Bus before the Peresandra Police for the offences punishable under Sec.106, 281 of BNS.
Respondent No.1 is owner of the said Bus, respondent No.2 is insurer and respondent No.3 is lessee of the offending APSRTC Bus, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 being the owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased and also dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.

Further submitted that, respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner of the APSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.AP-39-UL-6198 and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said vehicle and has issued Policy No.56050031231003391 and same was in force as on the date of accident.
Further submitted that, SCCH 5 compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly arbitrary and speculative.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2 being the insurer has appeared through counsel before the tribunal and filed written statement.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Respondent No.2 denied issuance of policy in respect of APSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.AP-39-UL-6198 in favour of respondent No.1 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased and also denied occurrence of the accident and death of Sudhindra due to alleged accident involving alleged offending Bus.
Further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH 5 6.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties this court framed following issues:
::ISSUES::
1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, Sudhindra B.K. @ Sudeendra B.K. S/o.

Late. Krishnappa B. died in the road traffic accident occurred on 11.11.2024 at about 6.30 p.m. near NH-44 Road, Reddigollarahalli Cross and Doddapylagurki Cross, Chikkaballapura due to rash and negligent driving of driver of APSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. AP-39-UL-6198?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?

On the other hand, there is no oral or documentary evidence on respondent's side.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased examined herself as PW-1.
In the chief-examination affidavit she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of driver of the APSRTC Bus bearing Reg.
No.AP-39-UL-6198, PW-1 got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch as SCCH 5 Ex.P.4, copy of seizure mahazar as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest as Ex.P.6, copy of P.M. Report as Ex.P.7, copy of notice as Ex.P.8, copy of reply as Ex.P.9,
copy of statement of accused as Ex.P.10, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.11 and copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.12.
On perusal of cross examination version of P.W-1 the manner of accident and involvement of bus in the accident is not disputed.

10. Per contra, except filing of written statement by respondent No.1 and 2, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.
11. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the APSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.AP-39-UL-6198.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this SCCH 5 tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Sudhindra B.K. @ Sudeendra B.K. was aged about 42 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have furnished copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.13 wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 20.01.1982 and the alleged accident was occurred on 11.11.2024.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.13 the age of the deceased is considered about 43 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 14 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others

P.W-2 stated that deceased was working as Assistant Manager in ECOS (India) Mobility Hospital Ltd., from 02.02.2024 and drawing salary of Rs.36,101/- per SCCH 5 month.

After deducting the professional tax the salary income of deceased Sudhindra B.K was Rs.35,901/- During the cross examination of P.W-23 regarding salary income of deceased Sudhindra B.K is not disputed.
Hence said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.
15. Further petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is minor daughter and petitioner No.3 is mother of the deceased, Sudhindra B.K.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar card of petitioners marked as Ex.P.13 it reveals that, petitioners are legal representatives of the deceased, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

16. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3, then 1/3 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the SCCH 5 deceased, so that, 1/3 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 25% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged between 40 to 50 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 against Respondent No.3 is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.52,06,056/- (Rupees Fifty two lakhs six thousand and fifty six Only) with interest at the SCCH 5 rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:30:10 in the award amount.

The petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.

On deposit of compensation amount, entire award amount pertaining to petitioner No.2 is ordered to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank in the name of minor Petitioner till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioner.
SCCH 5 The petitioner No.3 is entitled to get release entire award amount directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details.
Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
